report.summary: The strongest evidence supports Anker as the safest default brand, with the Anker MagGo Power Bank (10K, Slim) as the best all-around choice and the Anker 633 Magnetic Battery as the best wireless bargain if you want a cheaper MagSafe-style pack. The Satechi Duo Wireless Charger Power Stand is interesting for desk use and charging two devices, but it is bulky and pricey. I would avoid treating any listicle-only or affiliate-heavy recommendations as equally credible; the rankings below lean on hands-on and expert-domain testing from Wirecutter, Engadget, TechRadar, and similar sources.

products.name: Anker MagGo Power Bank (10K, Slim)
pros: Hands-on testing measured 10,000 mAh capacity, 15W total wattage, and one USB-C port for input and output.
It weighed 7 oz (200 g) and measured 1.8 charges for a 5,000 mAh device, which is strong for a slim magnetic pack.
The magnetic grip was described as strong, and it offers fast charging in a slim design.
cons: It was described as heavier than expected.
It is on the pricey side.
The slim form factor still does not make wireless charging as fast or as efficient as a good wired pack.
products.verdict: This is the best all-around iPhone portable charger in the evidence set: compact, capable, and backed by hands-on testing rather than hype. The main downside is that it is still a magnetic wireless pack, so it cannot beat a good wired charger on speed or efficiency, and it is not cheap.
products.best_for: Most iPhone users who want the best balance of portability, magnetic convenience, and real-world performance

products.name: Anker 633 Magnetic Battery (A1641)
pros: Hands-on testing said it can charge most phones up to three times with a combined output of 18W.
It includes MagSafe wireless charging plus USB-C PD and a USB-A port, so it is more flexible than a single-purpose magnetic pack.
The internal magnets were described as strong, and it includes a fold-out stand.
cons: The kickstand is a bit flimsy.
Wireless portable chargers can be finicky and most will not charge an iPhone at top speed.
It is an older design than newer Qi2-era options, so it is less compelling if you want the best current wireless performance.
products.verdict: If you want a cheaper magnetic iPhone charger and can live with an older design, this is still a sensible buy. It is not as refined as newer Qi2 models, and the flimsy kickstand is a real weakness, but the hands-on verdict still favored it as a wireless pick.
products.best_for: Budget-minded iPhone owners who want magnetic charging and a stand

products.name: Anker 10,000mAh Portable Charger (with integrated cable)
pros: Hands-on testing found a 10,000 mAh battery with an integrated woven USB-C cable, plus an additional USB-C port and a USB-A port.
It has a front-facing display for remaining charge.
It was described as relatively compact and pocketable.
cons: Integrated cables can be convenient, but they are also a failure point if the cable wears out or you need a different connector.
The source set does not provide a measured output figure, so performance is less fully documented than for the top picks.
It is not a magnetic charger, so it is less convenient for MagSafe-style on-the-go iPhone use.
products.verdict: This is the best straightforward wired option in the notes if you want low hassle and good portability. The integrated cable is useful, but it also adds a point of failure, and the sources do not give the kind of measured performance detail that the top-ranked packs have.
products.best_for: People who want a pocketable wired power bank with no loose cable to forget

products.name: Satechi Duo Wireless Charger Power Stand
pros: Hands-on testing says it can output up to 20W.
It can wirelessly charge two devices simultaneously.
It has a super sturdy phone stand.
cons: It is hefty.
It lacks magnets.
It is expensive relative to more portable and more common Anker alternatives.
products.verdict: This is the best pick only if your priority is charging two devices at once and using the charger like a desk stand. For travel it is not my choice: it is heavy, lacks magnets, and does not beat smaller competitors on convenience or value.
products.best_for: Desk use or bedside charging when you want a stand and dual-device wireless charging

products.name: Anker PowerCore 10K
pros: It has a 10,000 mAh capacity.
It can charge two devices at once.
It is considered one of the slimmest and lightest 10,000 mAh portable chargers on paper.
cons: The source notes say TechRadar has not reviewed this specific model, so the recommendation is less directly verified than the others.
It uses micro USB for input, which is dated.
It is not the most modern or feature-rich option compared with newer Anker packs.

specs.ports: 1x micro USB input, 1x USB-C input/output, 1x USB-A output

products.verdict: This is a cheap, established option from a reputable brand, but the evidence is thinner than for the top-ranked choices. I would buy it only if price and weight matter more than modern features, because the micro USB input makes it feel dated.
products.best_for: Lowest-cost buyers who still want a known brand and basic 10,000 mAh capacity

report.summary: Anker dominates the iPhone portable charger category across price points, with the Anker MagGo Power Bank (10K, Slim) leading as the best all-around pick thanks to Qi2 certification and fast 15W wireless charging. For MagSafe-specific users, the older but proven Anker 633 Magnetic Battery remains Wirecutter's top wireless pick, while the Anker 10,000mAh with integrated cable and the Anker PowerCore 10K dominate the budget tier under $25. Note that several major brands (Anker, INIU, LOGiiX) had fire-hazard recalls in late 2025 / early 2026 — confirm the specific model you buy is not on the recall list before use.

products.name: Anker MagGo Power Bank (10K, Slim)
pros: Qi2-certified for true 15W magnetic wireless charging — about 2x faster than older 7.5W MagSafe banks
Hands-on testing by Engadget confirms it charged an iPhone 15 from near-dead to 50% in roughly 45 minutes and delivered 1.64 full iPhone 15 charges
LCD display shows remaining battery percentage and estimated time to full/empty — far more useful than the typical 4 LED dots
Among the first Qi2 products on the market, with measured recharging time of ~2.5 hours from empty to full
cons: Heavier than expected at 8.82 oz — noticeably heavier than older 5K MagSafe pucks
Pricier than non-Qi2 alternatives; specific dollar figure not confirmed in our reviewed sources
Only one USB-C port (input and output shared) — no spare USB-A
products.verdict: TechRadar's top all-around pick and Engadget's most well-rounded MagSafe bank in hands-on testing. The Qi2 certification is the real differentiator here — you get true 15W wireless plus a useful LCD readout, and it recharges itself in about 2.5 hours. The weight and price are the only meaningful trade-offs; if you can stomach both, this is the iPhone portable charger to beat right now.
products.best_for: iPhone users who want the fastest Qi2 magnetic wireless charging plus a useful LCD readout

products.name: Anker 633 Magnetic Battery (A1641)
pros: Wirecutter's top wireless power bank pick, recommended specifically for iPhone users
Charges most phones up to three times at a combined 18W output across MagSafe wireless, USB-C PD, and USB-A
Strong internal magnets hold the phone securely during charging
Fold-out kickstand adds desk/standby-mode utility
cons: Flimsy kickstand that doesn't inspire confidence for long-term use
Older MagSafe standard (7.5W wireless) — significantly slower than Qi2 alternatives like the Anker MagGo 10K Slim
Heftier than modern 5K/10K slim options
products.verdict: A proven Wirecutter recommendation for users who specifically want MagSafe magnetic wireless plus a kickstand for Standby mode. The 7.5W MagSafe speed is the real limitation in 2026 — the Qi2 Anker MagGo 10K Slim is now a faster choice at similar capacity. Worth choosing only if you find it discounted well below the MagGo's price or specifically need that fold-out stand.
products.best_for: iPhone users who want a kickstand for Standby mode and don't mind 7.5W MagSafe speeds

products.name: Anker 10,000mAh Portable Charger (with integrated USB-C cable)
pros: Integrated woven USB-C cable means one less thing to forget — and you can use it to recharge the bank itself
Three ports total: integrated USB-C cable, additional USB-C port, and USB-A for legacy devices
Front-facing display shows remaining charge more precisely than LED dots
Observed sale price of $22.99 (down from $29.99) — excellent value for a 10K bank with a built-in cable
cons: Not MagSafe/Qi2 — wired charging only, no magnetic snap-on convenience
10,000 mAh is the standard capacity; nothing special for the size
No wireless output means you'll always be tethered to the cable
products.verdict: The best wired budget option in the Anker lineup for 2026 — the integrated woven cable is genuinely useful for travel and the front-facing display is a step above the usual 4-LED setup. Skip it only if you specifically need magnetic wireless; otherwise this is the cheapest sensible 10K bank from a brand with real independent coverage.
products.best_for: Budget buyers who want a built-in cable and don't need wireless charging

products.name: Anker PowerCore 10K
pros: Lowest-priced quality pick on the list at $19.99 sale (down from $25.99)
Three ports: USB-C in/out, USB-A out, plus micro-USB input for legacy chargers
Can charge two devices simultaneously
Anker brand has the most third-party testing coverage of any power-bank maker
cons: Not specifically hands-on tested by TechRadar — the brand is recommended rather than this exact model
No built-in cable — you'll need to supply your own USB-C
Micro-USB input in 2026 is a dated inclusion; most users will only ever use the USB-C in/out
Anker had a fire-hazard recall in September 2025 — verify this model is not affected before buying
products.verdict: Cheapest credible 10K bank on the list, backed by Anker's brand reputation even though the specific model wasn't hands-on tested by the sources we surveyed. The micro-USB input port is a tell that this is an older design — a sign it's been on the market long enough to mature, but also that Anker may be phasing it out. Verify against the September 2025 Anker recall list before purchase.
products.best_for: Ultra-budget buyers who want a brand-name 10K bank and don't need wireless or a built-in cable

products.name: Satechi Duo Wireless Charger Power Stand
pros: Wirecutter's pick for best power bank to charge two devices simultaneously
20W output — competitive with the Anker MagGo 10K Slim
Fully charges most phones up to three times
Super sturdy built-in phone stand (genuinely better than the Anker 633's flimsy kickstand)
cons: Lacks magnets entirely — you must place the phone on the stand, no MagSafe-style snap
Hefty form factor makes it less pocketable than the Anker competitors
Price varies wildly ($60–$100 across retailers); the $60 figure requires the Satechi promo code CPTS14
products.verdict: A niche pick — useful only if you specifically need to charge two devices wirelessly and don't need magnetic alignment. The lack of magnets is a real ergonomic loss in 2026, and the bulk makes it more of a 'leave it on the desk' product than a true portable. Worth buying at the $60 promo price; skip it at $100.
products.best_for: Users who specifically need to charge two devices wirelessly at once and don't need magnetic alignment

report.summary: After analyzing expert hands-on reviews from Wirecutter, Engadget, TechRadar, and others, the best portable charger for iPhone in 2026 is the Anker MagGo Power Bank (10K, Slim) — a Qi2-certified MagSafe battery that balances fast wireless charging, solid capacity, and a slim form factor. The Anker 633 Magnetic Battery remains a top wireless pick for its integrated kickstand and strong magnets, while budget-conscious users should consider the Anker PowerCore 10K or the Anker 10,000mAh Portable Charger with built-in cable. Wireless-only chargers like the Satechi Duo are best for desk use, not on-the-go.

report.summary: Based on hands-on expert testing, the Anker MagGo Power Bank (10K) emerges as the top all-around pick for iPhone users, offering Qi2 certification, fast wireless charging, and measured real-world performance. For budget-conscious buyers, the Anker PowerCore 10K delivers excellent value at under $20. Wireless charging adds convenience but trades speed; the Anker 633 Magnetic Battery is the best wireless option despite a flimsy kickstand.

products.name: Anker MagGo Power Bank (10K, Slim)
pros: Qi2-certified wireless charging at 15W, one of the first models to achieve this standard, making it faster than previous-generation MagSafe batteries like the Anker 633
Measured real-world performance: delivers 1.64 full charges to an iPhone 15 and charges the phone from near-dead to 50% in approximately 45 minutes
Slim, pocketable design (4.22 x 2.71 x 0.78 inches) with strong magnetic grip and LCD display showing remaining battery percentage and time to full/empty
Includes USB-C to USB-C cable and supports both input and output via single USB-C port
cons: Heavier than expected at 8.82 oz (250g), which some users find cumbersome for daily pocket carry
Premium pricing compared to wired alternatives; no integrated cable for emergency charging without the included cable
products.verdict: TechRadar's top pick for an all-around power bank and Engadget's most well-rounded MagSafe battery tested. Hands-on measurements confirm fast wireless charging (45 min to 50%) and reliable capacity delivery. The premium price and weight are offset by Qi2 certification and proven real-world performance.
products.best_for: iPhone users who want fast wireless charging without sacrificing portability; those willing to pay for measured performance and Qi2 certification.

products.name: Anker PowerCore 10K
pros: Exceptional value at $19.99 (sale price, down from $25.99)—one of the cheapest 10,000 mAh power banks on the market
Can charge two devices simultaneously with dual output ports (USB-C and USB-A)
Compact and pocketable design, described as one of the slimmest and lightest 10,000 mAh portable chargers on paper
Multiple input/output options: 1x micro USB (input), 1x USB-C (input/output), 1x USB-A (output)
cons: No hands-on expert review from major outlets like TechRadar or Wirecutter; brand is recommended but this specific model lacks independent verification
Micro USB input is outdated; USB-C input would be more future-proof
products.verdict: Best budget pick for iPhone users who prioritize cost over wireless convenience. Anker brand is trusted, and the price is unbeatable for 10,000 mAh capacity. However, lack of hands-on testing for this specific model means real-world performance is unverified; treat the rating as provisional.
products.best_for: Budget-conscious iPhone users who don't need wireless charging and can tolerate older micro USB input; travelers who want maximum capacity at minimum cost.

products.name: Anker 633 Magnetic Battery (A1641)
pros: Best wireless power bank for iPhone according to hands-on expert testing; comes closest to nailing wireless charging on the go
Strong internal magnets and fold-out stand for hands-free viewing while charging
Combined 18W output (MagSafe wireless charging, USB-C PD, USB-A port) allows simultaneous charging of multiple devices
Can charge most phones up to three times on a single charge
cons: Kickstand is flimsy and unreliable for sustained hands-free use
Wireless charging is inherently slower than wired; most devices won't charge at top speed wirelessly
products.verdict: Hands-on expert testing confirms this is the best wireless power bank for iPhone, recommended by Wirecutter. The flimsy kickstand is a real drawback, but the strong magnets and multi-port output make it practical for travel. Choose this only if wireless convenience outweighs the need for speed.
products.best_for: iPhone users who prioritize wireless charging convenience and don't mind slower charging speeds; those who want a fold-out stand for hands-free use.

cons: Integrated cable cannot be replaced if damaged, reducing long-term repairability

products.verdict: Good mid-range option for iPhone users who value the convenience of an integrated cable and real-time charge display. The sale price is competitive, but lack of detailed performance measurements means real-world capacity delivery is unverified.
products.best_for: iPhone users who travel frequently and want to minimize cable clutter; those who appreciate visual feedback on remaining charge.

pros: Can wirelessly charge two devices simultaneously, ideal for iPhone + Apple Watch or iPhone + AirPods
Super sturdy phone stand with excellent build quality—far more stable than magnetic alternatives
Up to 20W output supports fast wireless charging for compatible devices
Promo code CPTS14 reduces price to $60 (down from $100)
